NDT training in Des Moines: how it works for Des Moines employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training to Des Moines employers and technicians, either as live online theory, onsite at your own facility, or a blend of both, under ASNT Level III oversight. Atlantis has no classroom building in Des Moines or anywhere in Iowa. Your employer's written practice defines certification, a Level III gives the exams, and the employer certifies you. Agricultural equipment makers, fabricators, wind and utility teams and renewable-fuels plants use the training for MT, PT, VT, UT, PAUT, RT and ET.

Central Iowa's inspection work is driven by manufacturing. Large agricultural and construction equipment plants, castings and forgings suppliers, and hundreds of smaller fabrication shops make welded frames, booms, axles, tanks and structural parts that need production inspection. Around that core are utility wind farms and power stations, ethanol and biodiesel plants, pipelines, and a large state bridge network. A technician in Des Moines is more likely to spend the day on a production line in Ankeny or Pella than on a refinery turnaround. The questions an auditor asks are still the same. Is the procedure qualified? Is the person certified to the employer's written practice for this method and level? Do the records hold up when a customer's supplier-quality team visits?

Most Des Moines-area enquiries come from four kinds of employer. First, original-equipment manufacturers and their tier-one and tier-two suppliers, who weld to AWS D1.1 or to their own engineering standards and need production inspectors in MT, PT and VT. Second, foundries and forging suppliers that need MT, PT and UT on castings and forgings. Third, utility, wind and power teams maintaining turbines, towers, boilers and piping. Fourth, renewable-fuels and food-processing plants with tanks, pressure vessels and process piping. Each needs a different method mix, so we build the course plan around your scope. Request a Des Moines training quote and tell us what your people inspect.

Des Moines, the Iowa hub and Level III consulting: where each page fits

This page covers training for Des Moines employers and technicians. For statewide coverage, including Cedar Rapids, the Quad Cities, Sioux City and Waterloo, see NDT training in Iowa. If you need a Level III to write procedures, review a written practice or act as your outside Level III, see steel NDT Level III consulting in Des Moines and NDT consulting across Iowa. Many manufacturers use both: consulting to put the written practice and procedures in order, then training to qualify inspectors against them.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Des Moines

Every course follows the ASNT SNT-TC-1A recommended practice. Level I and Level II courses cover principles, equipment, calibration, technique, and interpretation against an approved procedure. Level III preparation covers the Basic examination, method examinations, and the procedure-writing and programme skills a Level III needs. SNT-TC-1A's recommended training hours and experience for each method and level are in our training-requirements matrix. Your written practice, or your customer's supplier-quality manual, can ask for more.

For a production manufacturer, MT, PT and VT Level II usually come first because they cover most weld and casting acceptance. Wind, utility and heavy fabrication teams add UT and PAUT. Process plants need UT thickness and PT. Tell us your product line and we will recommend a method order.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Des Moines, step by step

SNT-TC-1A is employer-based. A training course, college or state agency does not certify you. Your employer does, under its written practice. The sequence a Des Moines technician goes through:

  1. The employer's written practice. Your employer documents how it trains, examines and certifies inspectors by method and level. If you need one, see written-practice development.
  2. Formal training hours. Classroom or live-online instruction at the hours the written practice sets. Atlantis delivers this part. Minimums are in the requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience. Supervised experience in the method on your employer's parts, logged and signed.
  4. General, specific and practical examinations. Given by a Level III or designated examiner under the written practice. The practical uses real specimens, ideally parts that represent your production.
  5. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, at least annually as the written practice requires.
  6. Certification by the employer. The employer signs, supported by the Level III's records.
  7. Recertification. At the written-practice interval, by evidence of continued satisfactory work or re-examination.

When you change employers, certification does not move with you automatically. The new employer must certify you under its own written practice, using your existing records as evidence. Keep copies of your training certificates, experience logs and exam results. For the full employer model see SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Des Moines crews

Des Moines teams train with Atlantis in one of three ways.

  • Live online theory. Instructor-led sessions with a Level III, scheduled around production shifts. This suits individuals and plants that cannot take several inspectors off the line at once. See NDT training online.
  • Onsite at your facility. We bring the course to your plant and use your equipment and your production parts as specimens where the written practice allows. For a manufacturer, training on your own frames, welds and castings is usually the most relevant preparation for the practical exam.
  • Blended. Theory online first, then a compact onsite block for hands-on technique and practical examinations under Level III supervision.

Manufacturers in central Iowa often have seasonal production peaks tied to agricultural buying cycles, and utilities schedule outages in spring and autumn. We plan cohorts in the quieter weeks so new inspectors are certified before volume ramps up. Ask about onsite training for your Des Moines crew. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day. Manufacturers with plants in several states can look at corporate NDT training programmes.

Where NDT technicians work in Des Moines

  • Agricultural and construction equipment. Deere's Des Moines Works in Ankeny and equipment makers in Pella, Ames, Newton and across central Iowa build heavily welded machines. Inspection follows AWS D1.1 or company welding standards, and MT, PT and VT are the core methods. Supplier-quality teams audit tier suppliers' inspection programmes.
  • Castings, forgings and machined parts. Foundries and forging shops in Iowa supply the equipment, rail and energy sectors. MT, PT, UT and RT are used to ASTM standards and customer specifications.
  • Wind energy and utilities. MidAmerican Energy, headquartered in Des Moines, operates one of the largest utility wind fleets in the country alongside thermal stations. Iowa also has tower and component manufacturing. Tower flange and circumferential welds, bolts and drivetrain components call for UT, MT and VT. Thermal plants need boiler, piping and condenser inspection with UT, MT and ET.
  • Renewable fuels and food processing. Ethanol and biodiesel plants and large food and grain processors operate tanks, pressure vessels and process piping, typically under API 510, API 570 and API 653 inspection programmes. UT thickness, PT and VT are the daily methods.
  • Pipelines. Natural gas and liquids pipelines cross Iowa. New construction welds follow API 1104 and are often examined by RT or automated UT.
  • Bridges and transportation. The Iowa Department of Transportation, based in Ames, and county and city owners manage a large bridge inventory. Steel bridge fabrication follows AWS D1.5, with UT, MT and VT.
  • Research. Iowa State University's Center for Nondestructive Evaluation in Ames is a well-known NDE research centre. It works on new methods and trains engineers rather than technicians.

Radiation licensing in Iowa: a state radiographer certification

Iowa is an NRC Agreement State. The Bureau of Radiological Health in the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services licenses users of radioactive material and regulates industrial radiography under the Iowa Administrative Code, including a chapter on radiation safety requirements for industrial radiographic operations. Unlike many states, Iowa issues its own credentials for industrial radiography personnel, with separate categories for radiographer trainees, radiographers and radiographer trainers. Each requires agency-accepted training that includes on-the-job training, and the state's rules call for both a state examination and a third-party examination. Credentials have fixed terms and must be renewed. This is separate from your employer's SNT-TC-1A certification in RT, which covers technique and interpretation. Our RT courses teach the method. They do not replace the radiation-safety training or the state credential. Check current requirements with Iowa HHS before you or your crew handle sources in Iowa.

TWIC rarely comes up in central Iowa, because there are few maritime-security-regulated facilities nearby. Technicians who travel for national contractors to ports, coastal refineries or river terminals may need one. Power plants and some manufacturing sites have their own access and safety training, so plan time for those as well.

Method spotlight: MT and PT for production weld and casting inspection

The method pair that defines most Des Moines inspection jobs is magnetic particle testing with liquid penetrant testing alongside it. On a production line, the inspector has to examine many welds and castings quickly without missing a crack at a weld toe, a crater crack or a casting shrink. That takes a good understanding of magnetisation technique (yoke, prods, coil and central conductor), field direction and strength checks, wet versus dry particles, and visible versus fluorescent methods. For aluminium and stainless parts, PT dwell time, cleaning and developer technique matter just as much. A good Level II also knows how to tell relevant indications from non-relevant ones, such as magnetic writing or geometry, so the line does not stop for false calls. Our MT and PT Level II courses use production-style weldments and castings and teach the documentation a customer's supplier-quality engineer expects. For a wider check of your basics before exams, see UT Level 2 practice questions if you are also moving into UT.

Local options compared: NDT training around Des Moines

Many people searching for NDT training in Des Moines want a list of options. Here is an honest one, based on what we could confirm at the time of writing. Check details with each provider.

  • Des Moines Area Community College (DMACC). DMACC in Ankeny runs welding programmes, including content on welding inspection and print reading, and a Manufacturing Quality Inspection certificate. These are not full NDT programmes, but they are a common route into production inspection jobs.
  • Iowa State University, Ames. ISU's Center for Nondestructive Evaluation offers an undergraduate minor and a graduate certificate in NDE for engineering students. It is an academic route for engineers rather than a technician course.
  • Regional college NDT programmes. The nearest full-time college NDT programmes we know of are outside Iowa, including Southeast Community College's Nondestructive Testing Technology degree in Milford, Nebraska, and Ridgewater College's NDT programme in Minnesota. These suit people who want a two-year degree before their first job.
  • Employer in-house programmes. Large manufacturers and inspection companies in central Iowa train and certify their own inspectors. Being hired as a trainee is a common route.
  • ASNT Iowa Section. ASNT has an Iowa Section, based around Ames. Its meetings are a good place to meet Level IIIs, employers and other technicians.
  • Atlantis NDT. Live online theory with an ASNT Level III, onsite cohorts at your facility, written-practice support and Level III services for the employer. Atlantis suits manufacturers and contractors who need inspectors trained to their own written practice without sending them away, and individuals whose employer will certify them. Atlantis does not run a physical school in Des Moines and does not offer a degree.

Level III services and written practices for Des Moines NDT companies

In manufacturing, the NDT programme is usually audited by customers. Supplier-quality engineers from equipment OEMs ask for the written practice, qualified procedures, examination records, vision checks and training logs. Many Iowa fabricators and foundries have capable inspectors but a written practice that is missing, out of date, or does not cover every method they use.

Atlantis supports Des Moines employers with:

  • Written-practice development, or a gap review of your current one against SNT-TC-1A and your customers' supplier-quality requirements.
  • Method procedures for MT, PT, VT, UT and RT, written to AWS D1.1, ASTM standards or the specification your customer uses.
  • Examination preparation and administration under your written practice by an ASNT Level III.
  • Audit preparation, so your records are complete before a customer or registrar visits.
  • Outside Level III services for companies that do not employ one. See steel NDT consulting in Des Moines.

For the full employer model see SNT-TC-1A training and certification. Book a Level III consultation for your Des Moines company.

Practise before the practical exam

Production lines leave little spare time on inspection equipment. The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. The welding workshop scene is close to much Des Moines production work. See also Practical NDT in Des Moines.

The simulator is for practice only. It does not replace the practical examination, which under SNT-TC-1A is performed on real specimens with real equipment and graded by a Level III.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He sets course content, reviews written practices and procedures, and oversees examinations under the employer's programme. For Level III candidates, see ASNT Level III training.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Des Moines

How do I get NDT certified in Des Moines?

Under SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you. You complete formal training, build supervised experience, pass general, specific and practical examinations under the employer's written practice, and pass a vision test. Atlantis provides the training and can support the examinations and written practice. If you are not yet employed in NDT, a Level I course in MT, PT or VT is a sensible first step toward a production inspector role.

Can I take NDT training online in Iowa?

Yes, for theory. Live online classes with a Level III can cover the classroom hours your written practice requires. The practical examination is done in person on real specimens. See NDT training online.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your written practice and on whether you already hold UT Level I. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum classroom hours and experience for each level, and employers can require more. Current figures are in our training-requirements matrix.

Do I need a licence for radiography in Iowa?

Yes, in two ways. The company needs a radioactive-material licence from Iowa HHS, or reciprocity, to perform industrial radiography with sources. And individuals need Iowa's own credential as a radiographer trainee, radiographer or radiographer trainer, which involves accepted training, on-the-job training, and state and third-party examinations. Both are separate from SNT-TC-1A RT certification. Check current rules with Iowa HHS.

What does NDT training cost in Des Moines?

We quote on request because it depends on method, level, group size and whether training runs online, onsite or blended. Send those details and we return a quote within one business day. Get a Des Moines quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Des Moines employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the standard framework for manufacturing, fabrication, utility and plant NDT in Iowa. Some employers also ask for AWS CWI for weld inspectors or API inspector certification for tank and piping roles. Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A only and does not offer those.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA funding for NDT training with Atlantis?

GI Bill benefits apply only to programmes approved for VA education benefits, and WIOA training funds generally go only to providers on Iowa's eligible training provider list. Atlantis does not claim either approval. If you need those funds, check the VA's WEAMS search and the state list, or talk to an approved college. Employer-paid training is the most common route for SNT-TC-1A certification.

Can you train inspectors at our Des Moines-area plant?

Yes. Onsite training at your facility is one of our main delivery modes. We use your equipment and representative production parts where the written practice allows, and hold practical examinations under Level III supervision.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Des Moines?

No. Atlantis has no physical training centre in Des Moines or any other city. Training runs live online or onsite at your facility.

Which NDT methods do Des Moines manufacturers ask for most?

MT, PT and VT for production welds and castings, UT for full-penetration welds and forgings, and UT thickness at process plants. Wind and utility work adds UT and PAUT on towers, flanges and piping.

Is a welding background useful for NDT in Iowa?

Very. Many production inspectors start as welders, and knowing how weld defects form makes MT, PT, VT and UT interpretation easier. It does not replace formal NDT training and experience under SNT-TC-1A.

What do NDT technicians earn in Des Moines?

Pay depends on method, level, shift and industry. For a sourced overview, see our NDT salary guide.
